summary.text: Variance is a measure of dispersion: how far a set of numbers is spread out from its average value.
It is defined as the expected value of the squared deviation from the mean, and its square root is the standard deviation.
Its units differ from those of the variable, which is why the standard deviation is more commonly reported once the calculation is done.

facts.label: Definition
facts.value: Expected value of the squared deviation from the mean

facts.label: Units
facts.value: They differ from the random variable's units

facts.label: Two meanings
facts.value: A theoretical distribution or a set of observations

items.prompt: Two bus lines both average a ten-minute wait. Line A always takes exactly ten minutes. Line B ranges from two to eighteen minutes. Which has the larger variance?

options.label: Line A, because its wait never changes
Neither, since their averages match
They tie, because the totals are equal
Line B, because its waits are more spread out

items.explain: Variance measures how far values are spread from their average, and line B's waits stray much further from ten minutes.

items.prompt: A report on delivery times in minutes quotes the standard deviation rather than the variance. Why is that the more common choice?

options.label: It is always smaller than the variance
Its units match the delivery times
It is easier to handle algebraically
It stays finite when the variance does not

items.explain: Unlike the standard deviation, the variance has units that differ from the variable, which is why the standard deviation is more commonly reported.

items.prompt: A data set has a variance of 9 square meters. What is its standard deviation?

options.label: 81 square meters
4.5 meters
3 meters
9 meters

items.explain: The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, and the square root of 9 is 3.

items.prompt: Two measurement errors are uncorrelated. One has variance 4 and the other has variance 5. What is the variance of their sum?
items.explain: For uncorrelated random variables, the variance of a sum equals the sum of their variances.

items.prompt: A pollster measures how much opinions vary among 50 people drawn from a city of many thousands. What is this calculated spread, and how is it used?

options.label: A sample variance, used as an estimate for the whole population
A population variance, exact for the whole city
A mean, used as the center of the city
A standard error, used to replace the average

items.explain: When only a subset of observations is available, the variance computed is the sample variance, an estimate of the population variance.

items.prompt: A random variable has no finite expected value. What does that tell you about its variance?

options.label: It is zero, since there is no center
It is finite, but cannot be computed
It cannot be finite either
It equals the expected value itself

items.explain: If a distribution does not have a finite expected value, as with the Cauchy distribution, its variance cannot be finite either.
